Examples.Title: S-Parameters
Examples.Summary: A Touchstone black box swept for gain and stability, a pair of coupled inductors, and a FET two-port on the Two-Port Stability template's own Data Display. Stability factors K and mu are written as measurement expressions.

Examples.Title: S-Parameter Noise
Examples.Summary: Noise=yes on an S-parameter run: a 6 dB pad whose noise figure follows its temperature, a cascade of two amplifiers and a pad laid over Friis' formula, and a noise-matched LNA with its optimum source and two constant-noise-figure circles on a Smith chart. Every number is checked against a closed form.

Examples.Title: TRL and De-embedding
Examples.Summary: TRL calibration from a Thru, a Reflect and a Line measured through two fixtures, the two fixture files it writes, a filter de-embedded with them and laid over the truth, and a GaN FET de-embedded to its intrinsic plane, where Cgs, Cgd, gm and Rds come out flat with frequency. The measurements are synthetic, made by circuitRF from cells you can open.

Examples.Title: Hierarchy
Examples.Summary: A 9 dB attenuator built as cells inside cells: a parameterised pi pad placed twice on a board, simulated from a test bench, laid out with Update Layout from Schematic at both levels, and assembled in 3D from 3D views of other cells you can push into.

Examples.Title: Harmonic Balance
Examples.Summary: A 48 V GaN power amplifier driven into compression, and the same amplifier under two tones for IM2/IM3/IM5. The FET is a reusable sub-cell.

Examples.Title: Envelope (modulated)
Examples.Summary: The same GaN amplifier driven by an NR 20 MHz signal from a MOD_Source: ACPR1/ACPR2, spectrum, AM-AM/AM-PM and efficiency from one envelope run, and ACPR against drive from a sweep.

Examples.Title: Pulsed Radar (pulsed CW)
Examples.Summary: A 48 V S-band GaN stage driven by 100 µs pulses at 10 % duty from a pulsed-CW source: pulse droop from channel heating and supply sag, pulse-to-pulse spread from drain lag, rise and fall, from one envelope run. The device is a synthetic radar-class GaN model with a three-pole thermal ladder.

Examples.Title: Loadpull and Pursuit
Examples.Summary: The same device swept over a polar load grid (LP), and again with the pursuit search walking to the optimum (LPP).

Examples.Title: Klopfenstein Taper vs MoM
Examples.Summary: A 50-to-100 ohm taper solved twice: once from the closed-form model, once by the planar EM engine. Run the EM setup and compare.

Examples.Title: Patch Antenna
Examples.Summary: A 5.8 GHz microstrip patch with an inset feed, set up for a full-wave planar solve with a radiation pattern.

Examples.Title: 3D EM (Palace)
Examples.Summary: A bond wire, a via through a ground plane and a lidded package, each solved in 3D by Palace in minutes: S-parameters, capacitance and inductance matrices, and the lid's resonances. Simulate offers to install Palace the first time.

Examples.Title: 3D Package (the 3D editor)
Examples.Summary: An MMIC die placed from its layout into a lidded ceramic package drawn in circuitRF's 3D editor, with bond wires, ports and a driven sweep and the lid's resonance for Palace. Drawing needs no solver; the README lists the gestures that drew it.

Examples.Title: 3D Connector (booleans, fillets, STEP)
Examples.Summary: A coaxial connector launching onto a 50 ohm microstrip at a board edge: a housing with its bore subtracted and kept as the PTFE fill, a flange imported from STEP and united with it, and a centre pin with a rounded tip. Solved by Palace and by openEMS, with and without the fillet.

Examples.Title: 3D Wave Ports
Examples.Summary: How to set up a wave port: the 3D Connector's launch with its back end open and fed by a coaxial wave port on Palace and on openEMS, and an edge-coupled stripline pair whose four strip ends are each a terminal of a wave port on openEMS, plotted against Cohn's ideal coupled line.

Examples.Title: 3D Eigenmode (a cavity resonance)
Examples.Summary: Is there a cavity resonance in my band? A 50 ohm line through an aluminium housing whose first mode lies inside 8-12 GHz, found by Palace's eigenmode solve and seen as a notch in a driven sweep, and the same housing with one grounded post, which shortens the cavity the mode sees and moves it above the band.

Examples.Title: Capacitance Extraction
Examples.Summary: A pad beside a microstrip line, solved for its capacitance by Palace's electrostatic solver in about fifteen seconds: how to pick the terminals and the ground, how the Maxwell matrix becomes the capacitors a schematic wants, and each answer checked against a parallel-plate estimate and the line calculator.

Examples.Title: Test Pad Capacitance
Examples.Summary: A test pad on the far side of a six-layer board with no nets, joined to a 50 ohm line through a via with unused inner pads: its capacitance as built and with the pads removed, what goes wrong when the ground planes are left floating, and a schematic showing the electrostatic C reproduce a driven 3D run below the via's resonance.

Examples.Title: SAR: MRI Loop Coil
Examples.Summary: A 7 T surface coil beside a head phantom with every capacitor gap a port: openEMS runs once and keeps each port's fields, and a schematic then tunes, matches and optimizes the coil against S11, B1 and psSAR goals while B1 and SAR follow every value with no new EM run.

Examples.Title: SAR: Phone Dipole
Examples.Summary: A system-check dipole 10 mm under a flat phantom of head tissue-simulating liquid, run at two bands by a band sweep, with psSAR1g and psSAR10g at the rated power beside published reference values.

Examples.Title: PCB Component Ports
Examples.Summary: A 50 ohm line with a three-part pi low-pass filter, solved once with each part as a component port, on Planar MoM, Palace and EMerge. A test bench puts the parts back and lays the three answers over the schematic alone; change a part value and no EM run is needed.

Examples.Title: Antenna Co-Simulation
Examples.Summary: A meander antenna on a 45 x 95 mm board, solved once at five frequencies with each of its parts as a port. An EM Field Data block then gives S11, the radiation pattern and realized gain from a schematic, so the optimizer matches it and a sweep shows an inductor's error with no new EM run.

Examples.Title: Thermal: Die to Heatsink
Examples.Summary: A GaN-on-SiC die on a copper–molybdenum flange, a board with a field of plated vias, and a heatsink at 85 °C: the junction temperature and Rth against dissipated power, with the via field solved as drawn or as one effective block.

Examples.Title: Thermal: Channel vs Surface
Examples.Summary: One GaN finger under its field plate, and eight at their pitch: how much hotter the channel is than what an IR camera sees, the Rth matrix across the fingers, and a radar pulse through the fitted Z_th.

Examples.Title: Thermal: Output Wires
Examples.Summary: Six gold bond wires from a die to a package lead inside a mould compound: how hot each wire runs under DC current up to thermal runaway, under RF current at 2 GHz (the edge wires run hottest), and under the currents of a power amplifier's harmonic-balance drive sweep.

Examples.Title: PDK PCells (Python artwork)
Examples.Summary: A parameterised microstrip line, two spiral inductors and a MIM capacitor whose layout artwork is generated by Python, and a serpentine thin-film resistor. The kit ships inside the workspace.

Examples.Title: Via Contact Resistor
Examples.Summary: A thin-film resistor on a level of its own on a silicon back-end, contacted through vias, with a Metal1 line crossing under it that does not touch it.

Examples.Title: System Design (TX and RX)
Examples.Summary: A 2.4 GHz transmitter and receiver drawn twice — direct conversion and superheterodyne — from the System block library, plus a transmitter whose final stage is a nonlinear FET and a cascade gain/IP3/noise budget.

Examples.Title: Power Rail Integrity
Examples.Summary: A four-layer board with one 3.3 V rail: the DC drop and where it goes, Z(f) against a flat target, and which of thirteen capacitors are actually doing anything.

Examples.Title: Smith Chart (narrowband match)
Examples.Summary: A device input of 8 − j12 Ω, stated over three frequencies, matched to 50 Ω by hand with a series L and a shunt C. Drag either gripper and watch the band edges move.

Examples.Title: Tuning and Optimization
Examples.Summary: An L-section match, a three-resonator bandpass filter set up for minimax, and a FET amplifier stabilized for µ ≥ 1.05 while its complex source impedance is tuned by magnitude and phase. Each optimizes in under a second; the amplifier has one range drawn too narrow on purpose.

Examples.Title: Yield, Corners and Centering
Examples.Summary: A bandpass filter built from ±2 % parts and judged against loosened specs, an amplifier that fails one of six temperature and supply corners until it is optimized across all of them, a bias divider whose yield is centred from about 70 % to above 95 %, and an amplifier and spiral inductor, both Touchstone blocks, ranked in the Sensitivity panel. Every run takes a second or two.

Examples.Title: Layout versus schematic
Examples.Summary: A 3 dB attenuator whose artwork matches its drawing, the SAME board with six deliberate faults in its artwork, and an MMIC bias tee. The broken copy is broken ON PURPOSE — each fault is one thing LVS exists to find, and the README says what it is and what the report should say about it.

Examples.Title: Artwork to Schematic
Examples.Summary: A small board as a fabricator receives it — Gerber, drill, placement and BOM files — imported and turned into a schematic of lines, a bend, a tee and three parts in seconds. The BOM leaves one inductor out on purpose, so it arrives as a variable to tune against the design the board was drawn from.

Examples.Title: Schematic from Image
Examples.Summary: A picture of a schematic and a picture of its board, each made into a cell by Create Schematic from Image: the parts read from the pictures, drawn over them, and the values no picture states arriving as variables to tune.

Examples.Title: Model Composer
Examples.Summary: Device models built from data: a GaN FET from synthetic DC, pulsed and two-temperature S data, with a fitted network, ANN currents and charges, self-heating and drain lag, placed as an 8-finger device in a power sweep and a loadpull; a spiral-inductor family placed between two measured turn counts; and a model from a simulator's tables.
